title: Z.1 levels are not seasonally adjusted
Mortgage holders are apportioned
body: Z.1 reports holders for all 1-4 family mortgages, including business borrowers; the mart apportions them to households by each holder's share. This is a method, not a published Z.1 holder split for households.

title: Holding is not bearing
body: Bank-held FFEL, FHA and VA loans count as private, so public risk is understated; GSE risk transfer pushes the other way.

title: About 13% of liabilities are out of scope
body: Mainly nonprofit commercial mortgages and other loans.

title: Student loans before 2006 are imputed
body: A linear ramp from 1965, flagged as estimated. Without it, uncollateralized debt jumps from 7.6% to 11.5% in 2006 Q1.

title: Durables proxy
body: Vehicle collateral is proxied by all consumer durables, so auto coverage is overstated.

title: Buy-now-pay-later is missing
body: Mostly unreported to credit bureaus and absent from Z.1.

title: 2010 accounting break
body: FAS 166 and 167 moved agency pools onto GSE balance sheets. The public share is unaffected.

title: Fed MBS is rate risk
body: It sits inside agency pools and is never added on top; the agencies keep the credit risk.

title: NY Fed and Z.1 can disagree
body: NY Fed: a 5% sample of credit files, mortgages down $74B in 2026 Q2. Z.1: lenders' balance sheets, up $150B before seasonal adjustment.

title: Student-loan delinquency
body: Defaulted loans returned to credit reports in May 2025; the jump is partly re-reporting.

title: Z.1 revises history
body: Every vintage is kept; this site shows the latest.

title: Scenario presets are proxies
body: Bank loss rates from the stress test and the crisis replay, applied to every holder. The replay likely overstates the public share; leaving out federal student loans lowers it. Today’s balances in today’s dollars, not a forecast of defaults.
